done_when: An upgrade close syncs Forge's files without rewriting the repo's git hooks; close replaces the pull request's Done when line after an amend; a commit changing only close's test-state record counts as bookkeeping for CI reuse; story titles are read as UTF-8; an error during close's conflicted-merge handling aborts the merge and says so; command tests cover each, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Both parametrizations force `LC_ALL=C` while disabling UTF-8 mode and locale coercion. On Linux/Python 3.11 this also makes subprocess argument encoding ASCII, unlike macOS ([Python encoding contract](https://docs.python.org/3.11/c-api/init_config.html#c.PyConfig.filesystem_encoding)). After successfully reading the title, `_publish` passes its non-ASCII character through `--title` at `src/forge/close.py:600`; `repo.run` passes that string directly to subprocess at `src/forge/repo.py:118`, causing `UnicodeEncodeError`. Its `encoding="utf-8"` controls streams, not argument encoding. Thus both cases fail the Ubuntu suite configured at `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:80` despite the reported macOS pass. Keep the regression sensitive to implicit file decoding while ensuring the complete command can publish the title on Linux.

why: Real issues the coordinator skipped, still in close (audit, 2026-10-09): an upgrade close's full sync rewrites the real repo's git hooks, an amended Done-when never reaches an existing pull request body, a test-state change forces a full CI rerun instead of reusing the parent's, the story title is read in the platform encoding, and a SyntaxError during a conflicted merge leaves the merge active
